title: Every dispatch root takes the worktree fence from one projection, and the fence is one value that cannot be half-set
summary: From the architecture review of the fleet-rebase debugger fix (2026-09-28). withWorktreeFence sets WorktreeReadOnly and WorktreeWritablePaths for the orchestrator's live, resume and evaluate-batch dispatch, but two roots still derive the fence on their own: failure_learning.go builds the out-of-band retro request with a Worktree and no fence fields, so that retro runs unfenced (retro.go calls treefence.Begin with readOnly=false), and cmd/evolve/cmd_campaign.go derives WorktreeReadOnly itself. The pair also admits an invalid state: WorktreeReadOnly=false with writable paths set (cyclerun_remediate.go flips ReadOnly on a copied request), and the debugger prompt promises a fence from the writable paths alone. Make the fence one value (for example PhaseRequest.WorktreeFence{Writable []string}, nil meaning unfenced) projected by one function every root calls.
acceptance: The out-of-band retro dispatch is fenced like every other read-only phase, pinned by a test that drives it with a writing agent
Every PhaseRequest builder, campaign included, takes the fence from the one projection; a test enumerates the builders
A request cannot carry writable paths without a fence; the type makes the half-set state unrepresentable
priority_rationale: An unfenced retro can change the tree a later ship binds; a half-set fence is a latent trust-boundary bug
